name: Amatitlán II
summary: Outflow-zone extension of the producing Amatitlán field, centered on the Los Humitos crater northeast of the existing plant — a 175–200°C outflow plume fed by the deeper ~285°C Amatitlán reservoir, accessible at 250–650m depth within the crater, with a deeper ~190°C target further out. Outflow is structurally controlled by LiDAR-mapped N/NW-striking normal faults and crater-ring fractures. Current work focuses on confirming injectivity and refining the structural model with MT geophysics.
detail: Two calibrated temperature sections through the Amatitlán system show why Amatitlán II is treated as its own prospect rather than a simple extension: a steep northward gradient from over 550°F (~290°C) near the main field down to 150°F (~65°C) across roughly 1.5km (N–S), and a separate W–E section showing the shallower outflow plume itself doming up toward surface between two of its defining wells. Existing wells confirm the north-directed outflow is real and has shown no observed cooling since the main plant came online in 2007, but the land position supporting further delineation drilling is still small and being actively expanded.
